messages.title: Use Your Powerzone
messages.text: Keeping items in your powerzone — the area from mid-thigh to mid-chest — helps reduce strain when lifting, lowering, and turning.

messages.title: Use The Right PPE
messages.text: Using correct PPE :gloves:, such as gloves for proper grasping, reduces the risk of musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) like sprains and strains.

messages.title: Switch Sides To Reduce Strain
messages.text: Alternating between your left and right sides helps maintain balance and reduces repetitive strain.

messages.title: Practise The Team Lift
messages.text: Test the weight before lifting and use both hands. Ask for help if an item is too heavy or awkward.

messages.title: Stretch It Out
messages.text: Stretch before and after work to reduce fatigue and improve range of motion.

messages.title: Select The Right Tool
messages.text: Use the correct equipment in the proper way to reduce effort and avoid unnecessary strain.

messages.title: Reduce Exposure To MSD Risk Factors
messages.text: Test the weight before lifting, keep items close to your body, and take micro-breaks to stretch while working.

messages.title: Empower Associates To Participate
messages.text: Create simple ways for associates to raise safety concerns and suggestions. Ensure everyone across business units can engage.

messages.title: Close The Feedback Loop
messages.text: Provide updates on concerns raised and track them to completion. Follow up to demonstrate that safety feedback is valued.

messages.title: Promote Participation In Feedback
messages.text: Encourage safety discussions daily through digital channels, boards, and direct conversations.

messages.title: Dragonfly Program Features
messages.text: Ensure kiosks function properly, allow reporting from any device, and provide real-time visibility with manager follow-up through AUSTIN.

messages.title: Structured Feedback Collection
messages.text: Use skip-levels, Gemba Walks, VOA MyVoice, and safety boards. Track and prioritise all feedback for improvement opportunities.

messages.title: Recognition And Engagement
messages.text: Reward participation, use gamification, issue awards, and share positive safety stories.

messages.title: Encourage Reporting
messages.text: Associates can report concerns through managers, Safety Circles, Gemba Boards, scanner messaging, and structured safety programs.

messages.title: General Conveyor Behaviour
messages.text: Never climb over or under conveyors. Do not sit, lean, or reach underneath. Use designated stairways and never take shortcuts.

messages.title: Clothing And Personal Items
messages.text: Secure loose clothing and hair. Tie up long hair and secure beards over 3 inches. Avoid jewellery or accessories that may get caught. Ensure badge lanyards have breakaway clasps.

messages.title: Jam Clearing
messages.text: Only trained and authorised personnel should clear jams. Never climb onto conveyors. Use jam poles and report if a blockage cannot be cleared safely.

messages.title: Reporting Issues
messages.text: Report conveyor hazards immediately. Identify the nearest emergency shutoff switch and ensure it remains accessible.

messages.title: Emergency Preparedness
messages.text: Locate the closest emergency shutoff device. Keep it clear and know how to use pull cords and emergency stop buttons.

messages.title: Conveyor PPE
messages.text: Wear suitable PPE including safety gloves and high-visibility vests. Secure loose items and never climb, sit, walk, or ride on conveyors.

messages.title: Operating Procedures
messages.text: Maintain communication with coworkers, keep work areas clean, remain alert, and report unusual noises or operation issues.

messages.title: Prevent Cold Temperature Illness
messages.text: Bring extra clothing such as socks, eat nutritious food, cover hands and head, take breaks in warm areas, and wear layered protective clothing.

messages.title: Driving In Winter
messages.text: Turn on lights, adapt speed, increase stopping distance, clear windows and mirrors, and slow down in icy or wet conditions.

messages.title: Prevent Slips, Trips And Falls
messages.text: Keep your head over shoulders and hips over ankles, move slowly, wear traction footwear, and take care when entering or exiting vehicles.

messages.title: Stay Visible During Dark Hours
messages.text: Use flashlights and wear high-visibility or reflective clothing during reduced daylight hours.

messages.title: Be Prepared For Colder Temperatures
messages.text: Stick to designated routes, watch for falling snow or ice, dress in layers, move carefully, and stay hydrated.

messages.title: Prepare Vehicles For Winter Weather
messages.text: Check tyres, lights, windows, antifreeze levels, and oil to ensure vehicles are winter-ready.

messages.title: Recognise Cold Stress Symptoms
messages.text: Early signs include tingling, fatigue, confusion, and shivering. Late signs include slowed breathing or loss of consciousness. Report immediately and call emergency services if required.

messages.title: General STF Prevention
messages.text: Never run on the shopfloor. Keep your eyes on your path, avoid distractions, use handrails, and remove trash immediately.

messages.title: Housekeeping Best Practices
messages.text: Remove damaged pallets, manage wrapping tails, store equipment correctly, secure cables, and inspect high-risk areas regularly.

messages.title: Packaging And Materials Storage
messages.text: Properly manage straps, foil tails, load securing bars, and cables to prevent trip hazards.

messages.title: Cart Safety
messages.text: Do not push carts from the side or back. Ensure doors are secured and report stuck carts rather than using force.

messages.title: Working With Equipment Safely
messages.text: Avoid excessive force, do not attempt to catch falling items, and stabilise unstable loads before continuing work.

messages.title: Waste Management
messages.text: Use appropriate bin sizes, follow emptying schedules, and never leave waste materials on the floor.

messages.title: Impact Of Poor Housekeeping
messages.text: Blocked walkways, clutter, loose tape, and accumulated waste significantly increase slip and trip incidents.
